differences: The Ga (Yogev et al. 2005) part of the deposit has 29 patients and 18 controls with recordings, whereas the paper's abstract reports 30 patients (mean age 71.8) and 28 controls; the deposit gives a mean age of 71.1 years for those patients. The deposit holds only part of that study's sample, so these paper numbers are not used as checks.

The Ju (Hausdorff et al. 2007) abstract reports 26 controls; demographics.txt lists 26 control rows but one of them (typed with a different ID spelling) has no recording, so 25 controls have data. The 29 patients match.

The PhysioNet description gives 73 controls and 'mean age 66.3 years' for both groups and 63% men among the patients; with the 72 controls who have recordings the mean age is 63.7 years, and 62.4% of the patients (the description says 63%) and 55.6% of the controls (it says 55%) are men, so those numbers are not used as checks.
